searchText: Well at the end if there's an equal client distribution then there is no minority/majority client. So no advantages/disadvantages for anyone. > But I think it would have been really awesome if each team could spend some time evaluating another client different than their own. Realizing what others are doing and challenging at times if that’s even right or whether their own implementations Why the subjunctive here? Clients do this all the time. Prysm's monitoring from the beacon node was based in lighthouse's implementation. Pending attestations caches were tried in different formats and cross referenced among multiple clients for weeks. A quick look at all the GitHub repos will show active collaboration among different teams. I fully heartedly agree here. There is no compelling reason for single users to want to do the right thing. Even less so after having taken a path and committed to one client or another. And to make it even worse if you’ve built any kind of alerting based around one client’s metrics you’re even less likely to switch And that is putting aside the notion a lot of people have that if the majority client suffers a catastrophic bug a bailout would occur. We can say it till we’re blue in the face, past experience tells a different story What past experience? Did we not ship EIP1559 despite miners threatening to fork? Is there any example of Ethereum bailing out miners? Validators are not users, they're the new miners. <@340345049063882753> let’s not kid ourselves about the lingering ora of “the DAO” days. If you think this is a personal opinion go read some comments on /r/ethstaker There’s a general consensus that doing the right thing here might not get rewarded equally as doing the wrong thing when faced with a catastrophe As long as the wrong thing is more of playing along with the majority of the collective The DAO did not bail out miners. I understand people are having a hard time in adjusting to the idea that the chain isn't here for the benefit of validators but the truth is that it's not. Majority of validators is not necessarily the same as majority chain. but we've been over this ad nauseum at this point, so I'm not going to rehash the same points. 🙂 In the eyes of people The DAO was a social rescue. And the thinking goes that if something of that magnitude happens again social rescue will take place again Did not happen when Parity Multi-Sig broke and froze 513 774 ETH. I have a general feeling that people (especially devs) are strongly against any kind of bailout after the social madness caused by The DAO. That’s one way to look at it. But the feeling of average users of the parity multisig bug is exactly that of supporting the minority client You can even find comments on Reddit say excatly that to the letter. Where it’s seen that parity at the time was the minority client and because the multisig affected relatively small amount of people it didn’t force a social recovery to take place. True. If majority loses funds, majority will fork. But when talking about client diversity, a bug doesn't necessarily mean you lose all your stake. I'm not a core dev, but as far I know it's quite hard to get your funds slashed. It's more likely the bugged majority will receive 2%/5% offline penalties, so there isn't enough of a loss to call for a bailout. In that way, it's still worth it to run a minority client. Although this of course doesn't apply if the infrastructure cannot follow the right chain quickly enough. If a fork is detected, how fast can MetaMask etc. point their nodes to the right chain? If they don't do it fast enough, they will commit transactions to the wrong chain and switching back to the right one would cause chaos by reversing them. In such scenario, I think most people would just stay with the wrong chain as long it doesn't have any serious bugs. So I kinda see the point that running a minority client might not be the best idea. Especially because then the minority client will be slashed, as from the wrong-chain-perspective, they went offline. Getting bug fork slashed sounds way more risky than running Nimbus, Teku, or Lighthouse A very small minority of miners threatened to fork* Most of us protested but never threatened to fork. Although I admit I said a lot of stupid things as did others in the heat of the moment. And yeah Adrian is totally right validators will replace miners and will be surprised when they receive the same treatment. Can a single validator have >1 proposals in the same epoch? Also what about attestations? I noticed Prysm's duties structure for an individual validator in a single epoch has `AttesterSlot Slot` and `ProposerSlots []Slot` which makes me assume there can only be 1 attestation but >1 proposals for a validator in an epoch, is that right? you can propose multiple slots in the same epoch. You get only one attestation duty per epoch Is there a spec on how randao functions in the beacon chain? Hello EF consensus devs. If you guys don't mind, Can I ask how can I understand Post-Merge consensus process fully? Now I see the lots of articles include consensus specification, Engine API specification, annotated specification and etc, But I don't get clear mental model how Post-Merge consensus process goes on include execution layer side. Anyone can help for this? <@!915497547437576203> this provides some context: https://hackmd.io/@timbeiko/acd/https%3A%2F%2Ftim.mirror.xyz%2FsR23jU02we6zXRgsF_oTUkttL83S3vyn05vJWnnp-Lc%3Fdisplay%3Diframe Hi <@!552133098075193354> . When will the next AllCoreDevs Update be posted to medium? Probably next week or so. Waiting for this Friday's call.
